# Specification Quality Checklist: Distribute the Toolkit's Own Skills

**Purpose**: Validate that this feature's requirements are complete, clear, consistent, countable and tightly bounded, before `plan` is built on them

**Created**: 2026-09-02

**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.

**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Acceptance Criteria Countability

The reviewer asked for particular weight here: every criterion must state something counted, not something judged.

- [ ] CHK001 Does every measurable outcome state a number, a count, or a ratio rather than a quality adjective? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001..SC-016]
- [ ] CHK002 For each criterion carrying a "before" figure -- 74 references, 22 literal locations, 4 helper copies, 47 files, 6,148 bytes, 2 contradicting statements, 7 template files -- is the date and method of that measurement recorded, so a later reader can tell a measurement from an estimate? [Traceability, Spec §SC-002, §SC-003, §SC-004, §SC-007, §SC-008, §SC-010, §SC-016]
- [ ] CHK003 Is SC-002's count of 74 companion references defined precisely enough to be recounted to the same number -- specifically, whether it counts occurrences, distinct call sites, or distinct target skills? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK004 Is SC-003's phrase "instructions a reader is meant to follow" defined sharply enough to partition the 22 literal locations into those that must change and those that are prose about a user's own file? [Clarity, Spec §SC-003, §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK005 Can SC-005's "identical candidate set and order" be evaluated without running the four skills interactively, and is the comparison method specified? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK006 Is SC-006's "0 rules relaxed relative to the state before this feature" anchored to a specific recorded baseline, rather than to a reader's recollection of the previous configuration? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK007 Does SC-009's "exactly 1 of 5" state which field it counts, in effect terms, without depending on the reader already knowing the field's name? [Clarity, Spec §SC-009, §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK008 Is SC-012's "not traceable to a requirement in this specification" checkable, i.e. is there a stated way to enumerate the changes it counts? [Measurability, Spec §SC-012, §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK009 Does SC-014 reconcile its two counts -- 5 documents but 6 references -- or is the mismatch unexplained? [Consistency, Spec §SC-014, §FR-024]
- [ ] CHK010 Does every functional requirement have at least one measurable outcome that would fail if the requirement were unmet? [Traceability, Spec §FR-001..FR-027]

## Non-Goal Tightness

The reviewer's second emphasis: are the boundaries strong enough to stop this feature becoming a rewrite of five working skills?

- [ ] CHK011 Is "except where distribution requires it" bounded by a stated test, or does it leave the author to decide what distribution requires? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK012 Are the categories FR-023 protects -- questions, wording, step order, recorded outcomes -- exhaustive of what a reader would consider a skill's behaviour, or could a substantive change fall outside all four? [Completeness, Spec §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK013 Does the spec state who adjudicates whether a proposed change is distribution-required, and at what point? [Gap, Spec §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK014 Do FR-011 and FR-013, which require reconciling four helper copies into one, sit consistently with FR-023's prohibition on behaviour change -- given that reconciling divergent copies necessarily changes at least one skill's behaviour? [Conflict, Spec §FR-011, §FR-013, §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK015 Does the Out of Scope section exclude improving, refactoring, or restructuring the five skills' instruction documents, as distinct from excluding new skills? [Gap, Spec Out of Scope]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the boundary between "distribution requires it" and "this is a defect worth fixing while we are here" stated, so that found defects are not silently in scope? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-023, Out of Scope]

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK017 Are requirements defined for what happens when the host offers a distributed skill and a personal skill under names that differ only by prefix? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK018 Does the spec state a requirement for the case where the mechanism FR-009 depends on is absent, beyond the edge case that mentions it? [Gap, Spec §FR-009, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK019 Are requirements defined for the disposition of the four per-skill lint configurations found in the source, or is that decision carried only by FR-018's general rule? [Coverage, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK020 Does FR-018's "each file or class of file" define what constitutes a class, so that 47 decisions do not become 47 individual records or 1 blanket one? [Clarity, Spec §FR-018, §SC-008]
- [ ] CHK021 Are requirements defined for the placement inconsistency among the five test-scenario documents -- one nested, four at the skill root -- or is placement left unspecified? [Gap, Spec §FR-024]
- [ ] CHK022 Does the spec require that the distributed content's own statements about itself stay true -- for instance a skill asserting that a helper is byte-identical across three skills, which FR-011 makes false? [Gap, Spec §FR-011, §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK023 Are requirements defined for how a reader discovers that the plugin now distributes skills, given the repository's existing documentation states it distributes none? [Coverage, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK024 Does FR-025 define "confirmed present and invocable" operationally, or does it leave the confirmation's form to the executor? [Clarity, Spec §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK025 Is a requirement stated for what happens if the FR-025 removal is declined at the FR-026 confirmation -- whether the feature is incomplete, or the removal simply does not occur? [Gap, Spec §FR-025, §FR-026]
- [ ] CHK026 Are requirements defined for recovering the personal copies if removal proves premature, or is the irreversibility accepted and recorded as such? [Gap, Spec §FR-025, Assumptions]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK027 Is "resolve to the distributed copy" defined in observable terms, so that a reader can tell a resolved reference from one that merely did not error? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK028 Does FR-006's "deterministically" state the determining rule, or only that one must exist? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK029 Is FR-007's "that skill's existing documented rule for an unavailable companion" identifiable -- does such a rule demonstrably exist for each of the three dispatch targets? [Assumption, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK030 Is FR-008's "a test that holds under every install form" bounded by an enumeration of the install forms in question? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK031 Does FR-015's "positioned where someone editing frontmatter would encounter it" give a checkable placement, or a hope about attention? [Measurability, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK032 Is FR-017's "machine-local, generated, or binary" defined by criteria rather than by the single example the success criterion names? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017, §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK033 Is FR-021's distinction between authored and generated spec-tooling skills stated by a criterion a reader can apply, rather than by listing today's instances? [Clarity, Spec §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK034 Does FR-022 specify what counts as a source -- for example whether the host tool's own documentation is required, or any secondary account suffices? [Clarity, Spec §FR-022, §SC-011]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK035 Do FR-003 and FR-004 say the same thing from two directions, and if so is the duplication deliberate? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK036 Does FR-006's requirement to handle both copies being present remain coherent once FR-025 removes one of them, and is that reconciliation stated rather than left to the edge case? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK037 Do FR-016 and FR-019 overlap -- passing the existing checks versus the scope declarations still agreeing -- and is the relationship between them stated? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016, §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK038 Is the term used for the five skills consistent throughout -- distributed skill, plugin skill, vendored skill -- or do synonyms appear? [Terminology, Spec whole document]
- [ ] CHK039 Does the spec use one term for the record it repeatedly requires writing to, rather than alternating between "the written record" and "the record"? [Terminology, Spec §FR-013, §FR-018, §FR-020, §FR-021, §FR-022, §FR-027]
- [ ] CHK040 Are the Out of Scope entries consistent with the Clarifications section, given that one entry was replaced when a clarification invalidated it? [Consistency, Spec Out of Scope, Clarifications]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK041 Do the five user stories cover every functional requirement, or do some requirements belong to no story? [Coverage, Spec §FR-001..FR-027]
- [ ] CHK042 Are exception-flow requirements present for each hand-off the pipeline runner makes, not only for the general unresolved case? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK043 Are requirements defined for the recovery flow after a partially completed distribution -- some skills distributed, others not? [Gap, Recovery Flow]
- [ ] CHK044 Does any story cover the reader who installs the plugin and consults its documentation, as opposed to invoking its skills? [Coverage, Spec §FR-020, §FR-027]
- [ ] CHK045 Is the primary flow of each of the four git-workflow skills, invoked directly rather than through the pipeline runner, covered by a requirement rather than only by an edge case? [Coverage, Spec §FR-003, Edge Cases]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK046 Are the six recorded edge cases each traceable to a requirement that governs them, or do some describe a situation with no stated obligation? [Traceability, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK047 Is the mid-run upgrade edge case backed by a requirement, or stated only as a constraint on this feature's design? [Gap, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK048 Are boundary conditions defined for a skill that ships neither scripts nor templates, given that one of the five does not? [Coverage, Spec §FR-009]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK049 Is the assumption that the host resolves distributed and personal skills by differently shaped names stated as validated, or as taken on trust? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK050 Is the assumption that the host provides a way to reference a skill's own install location validated against a named source, given that FR-009 and FR-010 both depend on it? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions, §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK051 Is the assumption that the four git-workflow skills are correct as they behave today reconciled with FR-011, which requires changing one of them? [Conflict, Spec Assumptions, §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK052 Is the dependency on the repository's existing quality gate being sufficient as this feature's test stated with its limits -- what the gate does not check? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions, §FR-016]

## Ambiguities and Conflicts

- [ ] CHK053 Does the spec anywhere require a mechanism it has also placed out of scope? [Conflict, Spec Out of Scope]
- [ ] CHK054 Is there a requirement whose satisfaction cannot be determined until after FR-025's irreversible removal, making it unverifiable in practice? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK055 Are there requirements stated only in a user story's acceptance scenarios and never lifted into the Functional Requirements section? [Completeness, Spec User Scenarios]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Traceability: 55 of 55 items carry at least one reference or marker -- 100%, against the 80% minimum
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
- Two items were written because they name a probable defect rather than a missing sentence, and the reviewer should read them first: **CHK014** (FR-011 requires reconciling divergent helper copies, which necessarily changes at least one skill's behaviour, against FR-023's prohibition on behaviour change) and **CHK022** (one skill's instruction document asserts a helper is byte-identical across three skills, an assertion FR-011 makes false, which no requirement currently obliges anyone to correct). **CHK051** is the same conflict reaching the Assumptions section.
- **CHK009** flags an arithmetic mismatch inside a single success criterion: SC-014 counts 5 documents and 6 references to them. Both figures were measured, so the criterion is under-explained rather than wrong -- one skill's instruction document refers to its test-scenario document twice.
